notes.title: Patch 1.3
Nova's Diary #20 Still around
notes.content:
[b][i]Hello friends![/i][/b]


Here we are, a new Nova's Diary. It's been a long while.

You're probably wondering why we're here now.
[i]You're also probably wondering where we've been these past few months, and what we plan to do.[/i]


But before we delve into that, I would like to give a huge thanks to user [i][b]Sekoree [/b][/i]on behalf of Safe Place, for developing a solution for the infinite loading bug in the meanwhile. It shouldn't have been your duty to try and fix our game, but we were glad to see this act of initiative and selflessness.



Now, allow me to give you a little bit of a rundown from where we left off...



[h1][b][ RE: PAST ][/b][/h1]


After the release of Venice 2089 back in October, we were [i]admittedly[/i] pretty much done.

We had been working on the game for three years with little to no pause, so when it finally released, all we wanted to do was lie down, rest and find something to do next.

And so, while we were snooping around for opportunities, sidegigs et cetera, Venice 2089 [b]won[/b] the [b]Red Bull Indie Forge[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/26122e0ff2ca12b6eb7dc60699460dd82f71883d.jpg[/img][i](In the back are some of us in Milan, after a post-win interview in December 2022)[/i]


[i]For context:[/i] The Red Bull Indie Forge is a contest organized by Red Bull, open to all italian indie developers with the intent of promoting the italian indie scene both nationally and abroad. 

It was very much a surprise to us. Our competition was strong, and personally speaking, with much more experience and budget than us, so I didn't quite expect us to win.

[i]And yet we did. We won.[/i]

The next few weeks have been all about interviews and livestreams, as well as enjoying one of our prizes: a team of modelers, concept artists and VFX artists who would work with whatever we wanted for a fixed period of time. 
[i](We may or may not asked them to produce material for something we are working on[/i] 👀[i])[/i]


[i][b]So yeah, Venice 2089 is now literally an award-winning title.[/b][/i]


And while all that was happening, we also started working on a joint project with different schools in our region of Veneto, where after some introductory lessons, kids and teens created a point-and-click adventure type game with our guidance. Some of us are already working as teachers and educators 
 on the side, so this project was right up our corner... 

The game turned out pretty nice too!
It's a visual novel featuring a young student traveling to the past through videogame, where after meeting the famous painter Giotto, they work together so that the protagonist can return home and finish his homework that is [i](ironically)[/i] about Giotto.
Maybe a little cliche, but considering the game's been created by young students too, it's rather inspiring!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/c38dfdac0379d22b34a5143ca4109626aee39654.png[/img]



[h1][b][ RE: VENICE 2089 ][/b][/h1]


Now, let's talk about Venice once again.

First of all, sorry for how we handled the communication these recent months, especially when it came to bug reporting, but also generally engaging with the community.

Regarding bug-reports and fixes per se, the reason as of why we's been very slow in our response is that as of now we are down to just one programmer, who works on bugs on his spare time, whenever he's not needed on other projects. Our previous strategy of fast fixing cycles did not work, as well as our intention of incrementing our presence in the Discussion tab, therefore we rolled back to "fix everything wrong and push one big update"

That being said, we are working on that big update: a bundle of fixes and whatnot for the multitude of bugs and errors you all reported in these recent months. I know it's late, but still, it should fix whatever plagued your game. If not, tell us and we'll get back to it.

The update will come out [b]next month[/b].

And now you may be thinking: "Why are you making another Nova's Diary then?" That is because there are things on the way for Venice.

[i][b]Straight up, Venice 2089 is going to release on all major consoles.[/b][/i]

This was possible thanks to the support of Fantastico Studio, an italian B2B team that primarily works on porting games; they really liked the idea of Venice 2089 and we sure liked the idea of not only being able to bring Venice to other platforms, but to have someone else do that for us too, since we lack the personnel and experience.

Of course, it'll still take some time to finish up a couple of things, but the bulk of it is done, so don't expect to wait too long before being able to play Venice 2089 on Playstation, Xbox and Nintendo Switch.

Which opens up another argument: [i][b]We're most likely going to change the price of Venice 2089.[/b][/i]

This is mainly something that has to do with pricing in different stores, and agreements, conditions and whatnot, but it's also something that we pondered for some time after the release. Not that Venice is in a bad spot when it comes to its price, but it could help it being lower especially in console markets. Plus Steam has a thing for price parity.

We're still evaluating all possibilities, and I'm sure we'll talk about it extensively in the future. First thing we know, is that if a price change happens, whoever bought Venice at the current price will not be left in the dust...

Oh, and we'd also like to hear your feedback about it, so if you have anything to say about these news, do let us know.



[h1][b][ RE: FUTURE ][/b][/h1]

So, what exactly is our plan?

As you might have guessed, we [b]do [/b]have something going on.

We're still early in the process, so it's quite soon to show something. Plus we are also trying to make sure that whatever comes next, it'll be enough for us to stick around [i](and then some!)[/i].

Regarding the future of Venice, with the advent of a console release we had the possibility of coming back and fix some stuff, but in our current situation it may be that some bugs still persists. As written above, let us know and I assure you we'll get back on it as soon as we can.


Now, because of everything we talked about, it's very plausible that another devlog is going to be on its way in the future, but for the time being that's all from us, friends! 

...It feels good to get back to writing devlogs, I honestly missed it very much.

[b]Have a great June, happy Pride Month and see you all next time! 💜🏳️‍🌈
[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/faaf45c2400e752829ffd5a4584cded09fa072d4.png[/img]

notes.title: Nova's Diary #19 ...What now?
notes.content:
HEYO FRIENDS! 💜

It's been a while, hasn't it? It feels like ages since I last wrote a devlog.
And man did I miss writing Nova's Diary.

For those out of the loop, I intented to release this devlog much sooner, but due to illness (that I'm still recovering from) I had to postpone it by a week, which I honestly am a little sad about, considering that we've been silent for a whole week, and the release week at that! But hey, it is what it is.



[b][ THE DRONE'S OUT OF THE BAG ][/b]



Soo yeah, we did it. We actually released our first title ever.

Boy do I remember being all anxious on Discord (we couldn't organize a release party in-person, sadly), running all kinds of thoughts in my head to see if we did everything correctly and didn't miss anything.

And as much as I would have loved to be the guy that pressed the big green button that released the game, that honour went to one of our Programmers, Roberto, who is also the third person who got to adventure in this [strike]intricate and anxiety-inducing[/strike] wonderful and inspiring journey that is Steamworks (Just kidding, Steam actually has a very nice system, we just needed to get used to it :P )

But even so, it felt great. It felt great to see the little pop-up image saying that our game, a game where we spent 3 years of our life, was finally out there. And [b]WE [/b]felt great knowing that were people who were going to purchase our game and play it out.



I personally hope to feel this same feeling again and again, for the rest of my journey as a gamedev. 
And I'm sure I'm not the only one here at Safe Place Studio who shares the same hope.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/39759540567dc88b4aa361ba4a8c21e89e63aa20.png[/img]



[b][ LOOKING BACK ][/b]



Little bit of a history lesson for the new friends around here: Venice started off as a school project back in November 2019, back when we were still studying at a place named Event Horizon School. The first prototype didn't have much, it was just this young-looking character zooming around Venice with an hoverboard (and a yo-yo that could function as a grappling hook - rest in peace, gone but not forgotten o7), picking up the very very first iteration of vibes along the way. 

It didn't lean that much into climate change either, it was something that we added after hearing about the news of a record high-tide in Venice that happened that same year.

Anyway, August 2020: we finish up our studies and the first demo releases on itch.io. And damn did it went viral! Not only we were featured on the homepage, but we were also featured on freaking GXCorner of OperaGX! 

The hype was real, and only strenghtened our will to continue working on Venice 2089.

You can actually still visit the itch.io page, I just did and went down memory lane hard. Now that I'm thinking about it, maybe I should update it, y'know, considering we released the full title. 🤔

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/dd3b8e9f5385dae349d4f06567fe324ccb7d8f9c.jpg[/img]

With spirits high, we decided soon after to develop an updated version of the demo to put up on Steam, that released on January 25 2021. And yes, it's the same that it's still available today.

Man, 2021 was a wild year. Despite not having much luck in terms of publishers we were going full sails on promoting the game. We took parts in A LOT of events, like LudoNarraCon (Still the best event we have attended hands down - my opinion ofc), and thanks to our friends at Wholesome Direct we managed to attend to the Guerrilla Collective, where we announced our Kickstarter campaign!

...Except we had to wait like, 5 months for it to actually start? And it failed too???

Yeah, our spin at Kickstarter didn't turn out so great as we've believed, but guess what? To this day I still believe it helped us. Sure, call me a die-hard optimist, but thanks to our tank we now know A WHOLE LOT more about the ins-and-outs of Kickstarter, and the crowdfunding industry as a whole. 

Besides, it's not like we didn't find new fans along the way. For a team that was at their first ever title, without any prior direct experience in most fields, it was something!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/532bfdb989fb00b82dbdf7e9d56b8949fa7dc347.jpg[/img]

So we started 2022 with a renewed willpower: to publish the game, no matter what, in that year.
AND JUST THAT WE DID. In the meantime we managed to score at new events, talks, podcasts and even an internationally known event in Pisa back in July (I wrote a whole devlog about that if you're interested 👀). We still weren't finding any publisher for Venice, but at least we were starting to get recognized around.

At last, we found a release date. October 14th, 2022.

And I kid you not saying that we RACED for that date.
Not everyone was working on Venice, because we already were in post-production, so our focus was 110% on fixing what was broken, and polishing what was already in; but let me tell you this:

THOSE WHO STILL WERE, DELIVERED NOT ONLY THEIR 110%, BUT WENT THE EXTRA MILE!

And that brings us back to the start of this devlog, at October 14th, on Discord, waiting to press that big green button.


What a journey it has been. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/ea4b298996e81f36cae4c65df1e5f5aba1f1871f.png[/img]



[b][ LOOKING FORWARD ][/b]



Venice 2089 is finally out, that's great and all... But what's next? Do we plan on continuing to work on it?


[i]Yeah... Kinda?[/i]


A better explanation: I saw someone using the term "roadmap" in the discussions a couple days ago, and I fear that I may have been rightfully misunderstood when I said "Post-launch support", so I'd like to clear things up a little: 

[b][i]WE CURRENTLY DO NOT HAVE PLANS TO ADD NEW CONTENT INTO THE GAME.[/i][/b]

I'm sorry if you feel disappointed, I probably should have chosen my words more carefully in the note.
However, while we may not have plans to further expand the world of Venice in 2089, what we do have plans for is to improve the experience that people will have with the game, which can be done through bugfixing and further optimization. 

[b][i]...AND HOW EXACTLY DO WE PLAN TO DO THAT?[/i][/b]

Well, for starters... We are going to pull out the demo.

Reason is, and I'm [i]suuure [/i]you can understand, that it's a little... Outdated.
As I've written above, it basically is the same demo from January 2021, without anything new and prior to all the changes that we applied to the game.
"But can't you just make a new demo based on the final game?" I hear you ask, and while it is indeed a great idea, we don't feel it being our best course of action. [i](translated: we don't have the resources to create a new demo right now, and honestly told, we kinda want to start working on something else, at least for a while)[/i]


Secondly, is increasing our presence in the discussion tab. As of now, I've been the only one running the place, replying to threads and conveying bug reports and stuff to the rest of the team. And considering that we've received a generous number of reports since our release, I think it's better for everyone to have more people out there giving assistance. So you might see a couple of more people with the [developer] tag around the discussions.

[i](spoiler: they are all better than me at helping people)[/i]


Last but not least, is managing patches and bugfixes. We plan to catalog all current and future bugs in order of priority, depending on the impact they have on the game and their complexity, and to fix them accordingly, while releasing patches in cycles (we're still working on that).

For example, since release we've been busy trying to fix a big that caused infinite loading screens after closing and opening the game again. Bugs like this take the highest priority due to them being game-breaking (and in this case, save-corrupting too). Due to the gravity of bugs like these, as soon as they're fixed they are immediately pushed in the live stage [i](duh, what's why they are called hotfixes)[/i].

Right now we are working on fixing a couple more bugs (like the drone not working on some occasions and quest items staying in the inventory after its related quest is done) that have a slightly lower priority, and will probably release in our very first big Patch. 

So, as I said in the previous note, KEEP THOSE BUG REPORTS COMING!

Another (kinda secret) reason I like this system is that I can, if I want, tinker again with the dialogues. Thank the stars I haven't seen any typo so far (but I fear there might be some out there), but I feel like some dialogues could be improved over time, made easier to read. 

Because I know that I'm not an English native speaker, and there have been occasions throughout the development of Venice where I said to myself "Hold on, this is slang/not standard English", mainly because I associated a character with a particular set of habits (like Nova referring to their Grandfather as 'Pa) or because the english that I found in media I consume (be it books, video or games or whatnot) influence the way I write. So yeah, not a huge thing to think about, but it'd be a nice plus for me.

Oh, and as I said I'm probably going to create a new pinned thread on the discussion tab where I'll write the currently Known Bugs that aren't yet fixed. 

OH YEAH AND I'M PROBABLY GOING TO RELEASE THE FIRST HOTFIX AFTER THIS DEVLOG!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/d53d2614bf5a230d036353dfabe83694a4b47c3f.png[/img]


[b][ LOOKING FORWARD ...AGAIN][/b]

We're nearing the end of this devlog.

To be honest, I doubt that I'll write anything else for a long while, so I'm stalling as long as I can just to write something else lol.


...


Soooooo, I may have already spoiled the surprise a couple of paragraphs ago but yeah, we want to make a new game.

If you wanna stay up-to-date, follow our socials. For now they are all branded as Venice 2089, but I believe that I'll soon change that to our studio's name.

Venice has been a great journey, I already said that, but it's just the first title, the tip of the iceberg.
We want to keep working together, doing things that we enjoy, and making impactful games.

And I'm sure Safe Place Studio is up to the task. 



[i](too cheesy right? I can't help it)[/i]






I guess that's all then. Thanks for reading these devlogs. I look forward to write them again, in the future.

TrustAlpha, signing off.





[i](OK that was defo cheesy, borderline cringe. BUT IT SOUNDED SO COOL WHEN I READ THAT IN MY MIND)[/i]

notes.title: Nova's Diary #18 (The Pisa Special)
notes.content:
Hello my peeps, how are y'all?! 👋

Welcome back to Nova's Diary, issue number 18! 

Hey, do you happen to remember issue 16, May's devlog? That little rant I did about how hot it was around here at the time?


[i]Oh, how clueless I was...[/i]


Our sound designer in Milan says that the city regularly reaches 40° Celsius, there are literally milder temperatures in the southern regions of Italy!!

Oh well, I've already done my rant about temperatures, how about we take a look at what adventures July brought us.



[b][ FIRST PLAYABLE ][/b]

Aaaah yes, indubitably the best part of July.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/04376b3ac59f4ffa5fd02a53d3dd905f270f77ae.jpg[/img]


For anyone wondering, The First Playable was an event organized by [b]IIDEA [/b](The Italian Interactive Digital Entertainment Association) and the [b]Toscana Film Commission[/b], along with a long list of partners, sponsor and supporters from the game industry and the italian government. 

It took place in Pisa, the day after the Italian Video Game Awards (maybe we'll be there one day 👀), and it was the prime opportunity for us to meet developers, publishers and other important figures in the game industry, both italian and worldwide...

[b][i]Like man, I MET RAMI ISMAIL!![/i][/b] (if you don't know who this person is, go follow him on Twitter; you won't regret it)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/53d7ab76edb13ec4422781a3bcfd3725b6119634.jpg[/img]


Jokes aside, it really was a great event. Our main mission there was to basically do some networking, chat with some of the devs and listen to a number of talks and panels [i](which were very interesting btw, more about them in a minute)[/i], but we couldn't expect what was about to unravel in the coming days...

Great, now that I've got you all on suspence, here's a summary of what happened during the event:

[b]DAY 1[/b]

Day 1 was also the same day we arrived at Pisa. Francesco decided to precede us to listen on a panel we would have otherwise missed. After Fabiola arrived and we left our luggage at the hotel, we joined him...

[i]Too bad there was a metaverse panel... And now they even got a photo of me [/i]💀

After a good 20 minutes of time that I'll never have back, came the cream of the crop, the panels that we were looking forward to listen the most: a panel about [b]funding [/b]and the approach to publishers and funds [i](with extremely useful info for us and our next projects)[/i] and one about [b]accessibility [/b]and [b]inclusivity [/b][i](which was something that I really wanted to hear, also considering our main character)[/i].

A quick lunch and a couple of chit chats and we're back on with more panels: first of all, a surprise talk from Rami about game biz, who has probably the most straightforward strategy for game business.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/e0b135442df575ca004dc41a40357994dfc71cd2.jpg[/img]


After that shotgun panel we were feeling a little tired, so we decided to chill out a bit while half-listening to an Unreal Engine 5 presentation. 


In the evening there was an aperitif in this super luxurious hotel, where we had a really nice time (also the catering served something like fried bread and no joke it was delicious). During that we also talked with a couple of people from well-established publishers and development studios, just to say hello and show them our neat little game :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/1eb6f9f1514c7872367266a88771af99463220c5.jpg[/img]


[b]DAY 2[/b]

Honestly, what a turn of events this day was.

The second and third day were a mix of pitching sessions and coaching with even more publishers and other studios, organized thru this software called MeetToMatch.

Considering that our objective was to listen to the panels and do some networking, we initially saw little reason to go and pitch again to publishers that already knew us (also we didn't prepare anything in advance). But, surprisingly enough (/s), people like it when you talk to them, and right now we were in a building full of people with interests similar to ours and vastly different experiences, it'd be a shame to miss it all just because our first game's release is just around the corner.

And so we started talking with this incredible person from a studio that we already contacted months and months ago, and what a wonderful conversation it was. Sadly, our game didn't meet their criteria for publishing (which was something we already knew), but they were so so kind that they personally went and scheduled for us a couple of meeting with other publishers, as well as a talk with Rami!! 

So we went from a clueless bunch with too much free time to a full day of pitching and coaching.

Thank you Hollie, you were the best! 💜

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/0229ba490f69a8291db1bb4cd663cffacb415bb1.jpg[/img]


That evening I will forever remember it as the first of [i](possbily)[/i] many business dinners. 

We were in this beautiful villa, two steps away from the Tower of Pisa (it really is leaning!), And we spent the evening talking to lots of people, from their projects to a close-knit discussion about cats and anime. I don't think I've ever socialized this much since the first quarantine started.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/95eeadfc0b66da68389da27e6d4755479cde2edd.jpg[/img]


[b]DAY 3
[/b]
Day 3 was kinda slow. We tried to schedule some meetings but the people we wanted to hear from were extremely busy, so we spent most of the time chatting with other devs and talking between the three of us about the future of our studio: from projects to make to people to meet, as a way to kickstart whatever will come after Venice 2089.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/468d534ebc4f33cab5ece4183b7fa912ddef0f04.jpg[/img]

And that's it; after that we said our goodbyes, exchanged business cards, Discord tags and all the rest, and we went to the stations and took our trains home.

As I said before, it was a damn good event. I can confidently say that our networking mission was an astounding success. It was a shame that only me, our 3D artist Fabiola and our Game Director Francesco attended the event, as initially 2 other team members were to join us too. But due to the still-present coronavirus they couldn't participate with us. If there's going to be a new edition next year, I really hope we all get to attend it.

Speaking of coronavirus, guess who turned out positive after the event? 

A ) None of us
B ) Just one of us
C ) Two of us
D ) All of us


And the right answer is.... [b]C[/b]! Unfortunately me and Francesco were tested positive for the virus a couple of days later our return, and had to stay home for a good week. Honestly tho, I kinda expected it. The event itself was well organized in terms of sanitization, but when you have a couple hundred people all in the same place, these things tend to happen. 😅


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/568197e0fa7479a5cbf9ca0307bb937f5f7af8c6.jpg[/img]


[b][ THE REST ][/b]

Oh yeah, and we're still in post-production.
A lot of optimisation, a lot of screaming at Unity for not complying, and a lot of deadlines and milestones to meet.

And we're ever drawing closer to October...

And that's it for July. I know this was a very different devlog from the rest, but as I said last month, with the game in polishing phase I don't think there'll be much to show you, at least for the time being.

I hope that you liked my review of our 3-days trip in Pisa just as much as I liked being there.


See you next month!

notes.title: Nova's Diary #17 (The Not-Devlog Special)
notes.content:
Hey hey friends! 💜

Welcome back to Nova's Diary, issue number 17.
And man what a month it has been! 
[i](ah-ha, it rhymed!)[/i]

Let's get right into the heart of the matter: our[b] release plan[/b].

For the few of you who escaped my incessant spam (for which I congratulate you), back in June 15th we released a new trailer, thanks to our participation in the Shacknews' E6 event.

The trailer itself was a lot more narrative focused than the previous ones, who leaned more into the gameplay and the game's strong points [i](the 2D/3D, the chill soundtrack and yadda yadda...)[/i]; but that's not the most important piece: Venice 2089 will release in [b]OCTOBER 2022[/b] here on [b]Steam [/b]and on [b]Epic Games Store[/b].

Here's the trailer if you missed it, I promise it's the last time I spam it 
[previewyoutube=FCngmO3DFOQ;full][/previewyoutube]

Now, as much as we all are hyped for this, I cannot help but feel like there might be some genuine questions that you might have, and one in particular that I'd like to respond right now:


[i][b]- "DIDN'T YOU GUYS SAY THAT YOU'D RELEASE IN MID 2022?"[/b][/i]

Yes, back when we announced our Kickstarter run, we did state our intention of releasing the game in this year's Q2 no matter what. Sadly, because of the Kickstarter failing and the inevitable rescope of our game that followed, we ultimately failed to meet our word and decided for a later release.


[i][b]- "AND COULDN'T YOU TELL US SOONER?" [/b][/i]

We initially started talking about a reschedule at the start of 2022, but at the time we still felt pretty confident on delivering Venice on time. Later analysis and much, much talking later, we realized we needed to hasten our feature freeze to mid June if we wanted to have a solid polishing phase. 


[i][b]- "WHAT'S THE DEAL WITH EPIC GAMES STORE?"[/b][/i]

Very simply put, we are also releasing on the EGS.

Before jumping to conclusions, I'll assure you by saying that we do not have any exclusivity contract, and that there's not going to be a single difference between the two storefronts.


[i][b]- "ANYTHING ELSE WE MIGHT WANNA KNOW?"[/b][/i]

We (I) are fully aware that we've fallen short of our word, and that in hindsight could have done things in a different manner, but we assure you that we have only the best interests for our game.

If we have ANYTHING else to say regarding the game, I'll personally make sure to notify our community [b]as soon as possible[/b].


And that should cover all the questions, at least the one I thought of. Once again if you have any question or feedback you want to forward us, all our social channels are open.



[b][ DEVELOPMENT & STUFF ][/b]

Have you noticed how there are no more sections based on department? I figured that they'd be useless now that we're in post.

Because yeah, we're [b]officially in post-production[/b] now. June 20th marked the last day where we could confidently talk about new features; now all we are going to do are fix what needs to be fixed and polish what already is there, plus the very rare small addition to the game that we're 100% sure it's not going to cause any problems.

This polishing phase represent the last step in our development cycle, and it will continue 'til release in October.

...So what have we actually done this month?

Well, most of us were busy making the new trailer. This one has a lot more effort than the others and is low-key the best we have done, both technically and structurally.

The few others who did not participated in the filmmaking had a pretty extensive list of bugs and feedback that came from internal testing that needed to be sorted, or at least culled before the 20th. We started making builds like crazy, and you know what? Despite everything, we did some pretty cool stuff!

But as Mr. Bones' Wild Ride wisely teaches, the ride never ends...  



[b][ SEND-OFF ][/b]

And strangely enough, this is the end of June's Devlog. 

Can I really call it a devlog tho? Like, there's literally no images and it's just a wall of plain, boring text.

There's also another thing troubling my mind: what am I gonna do next? Continue with another devlog? Try something new and fancy? Only time will tell...

Aight, I'm calling it now. Issue #17 is officially named "The Not-Devlog Special"!

Before we wrap things up though, there's one last thing that I'd like to include...

What follows come from our Game Director Francesco, a member of the LGBTQIA+ community who was kind enough to help me celebrate Pride Month with a couple of words. Francesco and other members of our team are invaluable colleagues aswell as dear friends, and he helped me IMMENSELY throughout the process of creating the character of Nova.



[i]" Hi all! It's Francesco here, Game Director of Venice 2089.

Hope you guys are doing well. We are really excited to be close to the release of this little big game! 


When we first started working on Venice 2089, everything started with our main character, Nova. In our minds the objective was to create a teenager during a relatable period of their life: growing in a world menaced by big insurmountable problems while also dealing with the anxiety of just passing the exams (THAT'S A huge one!).

I think everyone can relate to Nova's apathetic attitude when the outside demands you to make choices and advocate for something, while on the inside we are struggling to find our spot in this world. Moreover, in all of that we are still probably dealing with our sexual spectrum, at least it's what happened to me. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/424591cc0599dcbb7bc745b6369bd4cb59c46ee8.png[/img]

Growing up I felt like I did not feel part of the world at all and the feeling I had was not only a matter of interests… I was not able to experience love with others as I felt like it was something far away for me, a teenager still dealing with self-confidence in being socially accepted.

Different story when I started university courses at art university in Venice: there being a weirdo was ok, and step by step I also gained the confidence to fall in love and experience my sexuality. But it was just the start!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/ee0213d9709088463bf31714c36b3b99154ae88b.png[/img]

Now more than ever I really understand how the confusion about my sexual orientation have always influenced the confidence in other spectrums of my persona; that's why I felt like narratively Nova would work as a non-binary character, quite not feeling to be part of a defined gender and still searching for answers to define themselves.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/4504dd3b0db9b8c5d91ef62171e8a86809755a09.png[/img]

As of now I define myself as homosexual… for the most part! I have to be honest: there's still some part of me that is still open to let other pieces of my personality and sexuality come out. Of course I would not identify my sexual orientation experience to Nova's sexual identity, but I would totally compare the feeling of being a bit lost and the necessity of finding your spot in the world.

Let this be my wish for pride month: be proud and be free. Don't be scared to share your feelings. Don't feel lost, we'll find our space together. "[/i]

[b]COMPLETING.
EVERY.
DIALOGUE.[/b]

notes.title: Nova's Diary #15
notes.content:
Heya friends! 💜

How has been April for you? I hope it's been good

We got a lot to show you this month, and I'll be doing this devlog in a slightly different way, (y'know, to spice things up a little bit). So any particular feedback about the format is hugely appreciated!



[b][ DESIGN & STUFF ][/b]

Let's begin!

Now, I could tell you all about the things we designers did this month, like updating the level design or writing EVEN MORE dialogue lines and blah blah blah...

But why do that when sooo much of April's effort were put into developing our main man [b]GIUSTINO[/b]!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/30caa008b635740f6b29649f8e0ad54ec4068756.png[/img]

So buckle your hoverboards, cause we have a lot to say!

So, a little recap for those who missed his story so far: Giustino started as a placeholder NPC back in 2019, where we used him while testing the first iteration of our camera rotation. After being ridiculed into oblivion due to his funny appearance for a period, he gained so much popularity among us (ඞ) that we HAD to include him in the demo, and so we did: he appears as a NPC during Rosetta's secondary quest in Day 2, as a shy gondoliere with a broken arm, waiting for his bread delivery.

Little did Nova (and so the player) know that was a 1000 IQ move by Rosetta to set up Nova and Giustino, because hey love stories are great.

Nonetheless, after the demo release we discussed on whether we should expand the secondary characters' narratives by intertwining them, something that culminated with the creation of a new quest for Rosetta in Day 2, "Food Delivery".
But that didn't have enough space for our boi Giustino, a character so well liked that we even started to meme on our socials.

And then, eureka! We decided to do a complete makeover of the character, from appearance to demeanor to even his quest!

Curious to know more about this new Giustino? Let's check it out then!

First of all, our idea is to have Giustino be present every Day in the game, either chilling around or being completely out of bounds for the player, in order to make him feel like a part of the picture. We're still working on that front, also because we are using this as an excuse to try a couple of new things regarding NPC placement, just like in this gif here.

I'll probably have more to show you next month, but I left some more info in the[b] [ 2D ART & STUFF ] [/b]section if you are really curious!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/aa96849e1c664df9015f43b3fcc73b32ec95b14d.gif[/img]
[i]first iteration using old dialogue lines. EXTREMELY WORK IN PROGRESS[/i]


Now, for the serious devlog.
What has been said at the start is true, there has been some update to the level design, with one honorable mention. Last month we've shown you our new holo signs, something that we thought could help traversing Venice while also seeming tech and traditional at the same time. Here's the new versions!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/c875e2f4fda6e9ecbb153d99cce023e3db649d36.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/f59822a252c2602246544247d446cc5e4aeaa3cb.png[/img]

Apart from that, we have something else brewing in the pot. Too soon to talk about it tho, so I will ask you to have patience. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/37f96cb9a4987c62bbd23b174a3a80cd3de4ec8a.gif[/img]



[b][ 2D ART & STUFF ][/b]

Great, time for me to hijack this devlog again to talk about our legend Giustino!

Relax, I'm only joking... Sort of.
Remember when I told you Giustino had a new quest? Well, in a nutshell you'll be helping him finding a job!

And what a better way to do advertise yourself but by hacking away soulless corporate ads?

Seriously tho, huge props to our Art Director Federico for creating such funny ads. There are a couple more different versions around, can't wait to see what you guys think of them!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/1a76ae50c0e59c87a80c68955b5e3b0564695ae9.gif[/img]
[i]"POV: You are Gen Z trying to find work in today's society"[/i]

Funny and relatable memes on the side, our artistic effort have been also used in A   W H O L E   L O T of texture recoloring and fixes. As you've seen on previous issues of Nova's Diary, our artstyle is our forte and is present in many aspects of our game, including identifying the levels of the game. You've probably noticed how in-game Santa Marta has a lot of warm colors, completely different from the cold, gray-green combo of Dorsoduro and San Trovaso. Last month we added our last Area, Punta della Dogana, one of the most well-kept zones in the entiriety of Venice, and we showcased it using the same colors as of Santa Marta. Here's how some of the new (and old) places of Venice look now:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/4b8651ab131f6a3a34a4da84c655133df9ee3d9a.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/8aefe60014ea3c1c2e62f6e7795801ad852175ca.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/05c8273b124ca39f29169dc63276595977c3605c.png[/img]
[i]"Remember when this place used to be all brown? We do"[/i]



[b][3D ART & STUFF ][/b]

Sadly we don't have much to show for 3D this month, but nonetheless we can showcase you something, like the brand new Leo's Den!

Leo's Den is basically what you would call Leo's Alley during the High Tide, so much as it is placed in the exact same position! It makes an appearance during Day 4. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/7edc379bf6e6f013944229fd47198893eae741df.png[/img]

And another thing that I'll keep mentioning from time to time in our "level design updates" is the introduction of "Tiranti", or guy-wires as you may know them.

These bad boys have been used all over Venice since ever, to bear the weight of crooked buildings and as a primitive anti-seismic tool

How do they work exactly? As far as I can tell, you basically put an iron bar inside a building (I dunno I'm not an architect).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/326f99d2fce2a95d31004179162a6d24a6003365.png[/img]


[b][ PROGRAMMING & STUFF ][/b]

As usual, our programmers have been hard at work smashing bugs left and right, but it does not stop there!

Due to our numerous recent additions to the game both in editor and in code, performance has been kinda fluctuating therefore we also worked on some more optimisations, making sure our game won't eat 100% of your CPU.

Oh and we made a save/load system.

...

[i]"...W-What? PROGRAMMING HAS SOMETHING FOR ONCE?!?!?" - All of you right now[/i]

That's right! Now, you may be wondering why such an important feature in User Experience (UX) has been just recently added: Initially we thought of introducing a full-fledged saving/loading system waaay back in 2020. After the demo release, due to the feedback we were receiving about the lenght of the demo and the inability to save we considered the possibility of releasing a patch [i](something we haven't really felt like doing for just a demo)[/i]. 

But since at the same time we started on working on major parts of the game [i](namely the vibes rework)[/i] that needed the full attention of our programmers, the idea was put on hold. 

Until now, at least.

tl,dr: Few programmers, lotta stuff. Prioritisation.



[b][ SEND-OFFS ][/b]

And that's a wrap for our April Nova's Diary!

As usual, hope you all enjoyed the read about the bizarre things that happen behind the scenes of Venice 2089. Did you like getting to know the background of Giustino? Y'know, It kinda makes me wanna do it every month for every character... I'll look into that.
If you have ANYTHING you wanna say to us, feel free! We'll be seeing you next month!


Now go tell your friends to wishlist the game.

Tell 'em to play the demo too.


[b]Do it for him.[/b]

notes.title: Nova's Diary #14
notes.content:
Heyo friends! 💜

Welcome once again to Nova's Diary, issue number... *check notes* 14 already?!? 

Spring has arrived! No better time to jump on the myriad of things we've done this month!


[b][ DESIGN & STUFF ][/b]

Given that it's springtime, this naturally means it's time for spring cleaning!

Now, before you [i]comprehensibly[/i] come at me with torches and pitchforks for [b]YET [/b]another month of "design updates", let me lull you by saying that it's not just bugsmashing that we've done this month: A whole plethora of design subjects have been discussed, changed and improved, and I'm going to show you the best bits!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/034646c0054580f68427529816b41c547652e914.png[/img]

Ta-Dah! A brand new image of the final Area, named [b]Punta della Dogana[/b]. Unlike Santa Marta and Inner Dorsoduro, Punta della Dogana is much cleaner and well taken care of, considering it houses some of the more important administrative buildings of the city, as well as some of the few remaining monuments and landmarks.

It is introduced in the final arc of the game, and it features its own NPCs, quests and whatnot.
(I would love to share more with you but as you know, this is pretty endgame and I wouldn't want to spoil the end for you)


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/6d2260d91baa85affad79301fbeb6f0bfba854d6.png[/img]

Hey, doesn't that holo-sign look familiar? Yes it does!

One issue we noticed during playtests was that it was very difficult for new players to navigate Venice during the High Tide; most of the signs are submerged during this time, and with the pathing changes it makes for a difficult, albeit fresh experience for players that are still trying to memorize the level design. On top of that, we still believe we can add a little more "tech" into our future Venice, so we started thinking about an hybrid version of signage based on the traditional ones you'd find in Venice today [i](and hopefully in our 2089 too)[/i], but holo!

It's still our first iteration and it's probably going to get a lot of changes, but hopefully this new way of orientation (paired with some big-brain placement) will help players have an easier time exploring Venice!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/cdbad15ec76888ea5a2348bc9137e26386209ef8.png[/img]

This one isn't that big of a thing, but I very much like it and it deserves its own spot

Along with the new holo-signs, we also discussed on what other technological elements we could add into the level to better sell the "2089 but not that futuristic" vibe, and honestly [i]WHAT BETTER CHOICE THAN A BUNCH OF ANTENNAE![/i]

They are the perfect element of old-tech in a place that doesn't match the current year, almost like it's timelost, that is our brick-built, bright coloured Venice. Besides, they are so common throughout Italy (even to this day!) that if you've ever been to Venice, if you'd look up on the rooftops, they'd be filled with a mix of dishes and antennas. 

They are easy to make, pose little to no problem from an optimization standpoint, and embellish the view during the High Tide!



Another thing I wanted to add to the design section is my intention of updating the game's Steam Page soon. Back when I made it, in December 2020, I basically speedrunned it, and so made it very similar to our Itch.io and Gamejolt counterparts [i](which at the time were booming, soo I thought "hey, this must be the way to go!")[/i]

But a year later and nearing release, it's kinda... Meh...

I feel there could be much more personality in our page, that can be shown for example by putting better gifs [i](the first ones do have a compression issue)[/i], or updating the texts [i](now everybody and their dogs know what's written in there)[/i] and generally changing the layout, in order to make it less...Google Docs-like?

Oh yeah, and change whatever outdated info is there. It may be correct for our demo, but for the full-fledge game I'd like to have solid information of the actual official build, rather than our 2020 demo release, you know?


I dunno, I have to consult my fellow designers and a couple of artists too, luckily it's not that urgent of an issue. But [b]SOON™[/b] there shall be a shiny new Venice 2089 Steam Page!

Oh, and if you have any feedback, idea or suggestion about how should I shape the new page, I'm all ears, let me know 🤗

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/507ac3503d07741078fddb635627e385aac3cae0.jpg[/img]


[b][ 2D ART & STUFF ][/b]


The spring cleaning saga continues! 
While most of March has been an updating month for our artists (yes, even artists do that), there is one piece of content that I really want to show you!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/1b4795d6674e377533006bef899758b8941dd367.png[/img]

Made by our master artist (AKA Art Director) Federico, these terrific graffiti are very much different from the ones normally found, and pack a serious punch to the gut in terms of worldbuilding. 

Back when planning the narrative ecosystem of Venice 2089, I always wanted Venice to feel like a "lived in" city, and with the countless events that happened before the start of the game, it'd be natural to have some sort of evidence of what happened and what meant for the people of Venice....

These works, made a very long time ago by an unnamed artist, show the cold reality of the times before Nova, and to this day stand as a memento of the discomfort and worry of the citizen of those times.

One might say it even encouraged a certain rebellious artist to start expressing his feelings with spray paint...



[b][ 3D ART & STUFF ][/b]

Not much to be said about 3D this month, other than the madlads managed to do us a big favour by downscaling the textures of half the models of Venice [i](it means that Venice won't be a 40 gigs game lol)[/i]

Apart from that, they worked close with us designers in finalizing Punta della Dogana, and created a couple more variations of our loved altane for the High Tide, in order to bring some more variety both visually and mechanically!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/d0455a342a41995b14b19c30dd2c2c923dfc3076.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/8c550f35d45bc02d5222739b5e41027e0902cf79.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/561e9d5997f63cc401445162da4e7fcbfa614243.png[/img]


[b][ PROGRAMMING & STUFF ][/b]

...You really want me to comment the programming section of the now known "Month of Updates?"

Jokes aside, nothing terribly groundbreaking happened, lots of optimization has indeed happened and now the game runs smoother as ever!

Will update when the big news will arrive 


[b][ SEND OFF ][/b]

And that's about it. Holy moly what a long devlog, it's been ages since I had a design section that verbose!

Honestly though, we're just that close to finishing Venice, and let me tell you [i]WE ALL FEEL IT[/i], the hype is real!

Thanks for sticking with our devlogs, thanks for interacting with us here on Steam or on our social platforms, and I cannot wait to hear more of you guys!

See you next month!

Yesterday we reminisced the past of Venice 2089 and our accomplishments, today we are going to have a little more in depth look on what we've been working on these last two months.

Prepare to be disappointed, 'cause there isn't much to show you....
BUT, do you happen to know how two months full of meddling with Unity look like? Trust me, they're especially [i]exhausting.[/i]
We spent two whole months mainly on optimization, trying out or tuning different methods to make the game run better on mid-end and low-end rigs, while also finishing up some world design stuff we left behind in the previous months.

For that we started developing internal builds more often, to better focus on our schedule and group together the stream of progress made by other departments.

Oh and in December, consider we were still running the Kickstarter campaign so a couple of us (me mainly) were still working more on that front rather than our other design duties.

Sooo yeah, boring stuff with next to nothing to share.
I'll think of something for the next issues, I promise.


[b][ 2D & STUFF ][/b]

notes.title: Nova's Diary #?? - 1 YEAR SPECIAL
notes.content:
Hello friends 💜

Happy [i](super-late)[/i] New Year!!! Here's to a 2022 full of great things and good vibes!

[b][ 2021 RECAP ][/b]

Now, this is not our usual devlog [i](it never is but anyway)[/i], because today it has been [b]EXACTLY a year[/b] since our demo release here on Steam, and I think some celebreations are due :)

It's crazy to think that just about two years ago, Venice 2089 was already on route to become something bigger than just a school project; true, we had a fairly solid demo release on Itch.io and GameJolt and our spirits were high and we were eager to continue development, yet it took just a couple of months of work to substantially enhance that demo and release it on Steam, where the real journey started. And honestly, what a journey it has been so far...

We participated in wonderful events such as 2021's [b]LudoNarraCon [/b](something that we really hoped to do) and [b]NowPlayThis[/b] and [b]DreamHack Beyond[/b], where we had the possibility to directly speak about our vision for the future of the game.

We had the privilege of being in the pre-show of both [b]E3 [/b]and [b]The Game Awards[/b], thanks to [b]Guerrilla Collective[/b] and [b]Future of Play[/b], where we announced our intention of running a Kickstarter campaign.

We started nurturing our online image, started growing a community on social media fueled by dev news and memes.

We had interviews, meetings and so on. We became a full-fledged studio.

We even got to participate in a in-person convention here in Italy, with our own little stand.

Even when things became a little bleak with our Kickstarter, we kept on going.
[i](also thanks to your support)[/i]

All the while creating, improving and fine-tuning this [strike]not-so[/strike] little work of ours for you to enjoy...
And all of this in just a single year. If that doesn't scream progress, I dunno what does

So yeah, here's  for an astounding 2021!


[b][ THE BIG ADVENTURE EVENT ][/b]

Oh, and one veeery recent but worthy addition is our participation in [b]"The Big Adventure Event"[/b] AKA BAE, made by those wonderful people at Hitcents. It was a really neat event and as always we had a blast (minus some technical difficulties lol).

We even did an art stream featuring our Art Director Federico, just like the first stream we ever did! 

Events such as this are really helpful to us in terms of discoverability and word of mouth, and for a title like ours having like-minded players see our game and trying it out it's better than just showcasing a trailer in a bigger, broader event. So thank you to those of you who have participated in our stream, tried our game and gave us feedback.  


Besides, we get to catch up and see what other fellow indie devs are working on, and let me tell you: there are some real bangers in the works 👀


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/8c18cccb44c246d6388f07c9b5aa03e4be274e84.png[/img]





[b][ SEND-OFF ][/b]

And that's that, the conclusion of a great year and the start of a [i](hopefully)[/i] even greater one.

Seriously, I cannot stress this enough: THANK YOU FOR SUPPORTING US, even if it's just having your wishlist on or retweeting our funny images (and for reading through these devlogs of mine if you are one of those people).

The real devlog will be out tomorrow, and it will cover both December and January.

See you tomorrow!

notes.title: Nova's Diary #8
notes.content:
Hello friends 💜,

Autumn's cometh, and it's time already for a new issue of Nova's Diary! And a special one too, because we recently passed our first(ish) anniversary of development; and as such, we wanted to celebrate it by answering some questions, mainly regarding the project itself and the long-due Kickstarter:

[i][b]"OI, IT'S BEEN 3 MONTHS ALREADY! WHERE HAVE YOU BEEN?[/b][/i]

Well... Here! We've been hard at work (and still are!), fleshing out the game and adding content, while 
simultaneously continuing the search for a publisher/fund/someone willing to help us through funding or 
assistance. Alas, the search for now hasn't yielded great results for us, leading the way for alternative solutions such as Kickstarter.


[i][b]"UH THAT'S GREAT, BUT WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED TO IT?[/b][/i]

We thought that announcing the Kickstarter opening during E3's Guerrilla Collective was the better 
course of action (spoiler: it was). What we DIDN'T thought was how lenghty and tedious some legal preparations were. Just days before the opening we run into some difficulties that made really really hard for us for continue with our plan without messing up something later on, so we unanimously decided to hold back the opening until those issues had been fixed.

On the positive, as of recentl days we finally have our situation 100% clear and thanks to our legal team, we expect things to return to normal somewhere before the end of the year.


[i][b]"SO, THE GAME'S STILL COMING TO KICKSTARTER RIGHT?"[/b][/i]

That's right! As soon as those pesky difficulties are settled, we'll open up the Kickstarter campaign! 
We'll probably have to rethink a couple of goals and reward tiers too, but most of the structure is already in place! But what if it fails?

Most likely we'll go sulk in the corner for a bit, and then we'll resume development as usual. As we repeatedly stated, our ABSOLUTE priority is to finish the game and deliver it to Steam in its best condition, although production time will inevitably be lenghtened and we'll have to cut content to make sure the game comes out.


[b][i]"AND WHEN WILL THE GAME OFFICIALLY LAUNCH?"[/i][/b]

Our final, stone-set deadline is Q2 2022. 


Great, now that I have successfully submerged you with too many words, let's head over to the actual devlog...

Work has gone into the implementation of our main quests into said Days, while also putting some thought in fixing/reworking some old structures/mechanics that we no longer use.

Also, we begun working on something special, that you guys will probably see very soon... 👀

You can say that his looks are rather...Unique, but stay sure that what he lacks in aesthetics he makes up with personality and charm [strike]/s[/strike]. Another thing artists have been busy with was working with us designers in creating the second puzzle from prototypes, and the final result is very much like we first imagined it!

You know 'em, you love 'em: trees once again! Huge progress has been made in the shader creation, so much that we even begun testing on other type of trees! [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/284865c36b3c700148965dce554168047e2010bc.png[/img]

[b]3D ART & STUFF[/b]

Sadly, I don't have much to show regarding 3D this month, as our modelers and texturers took the opportunity to go on vacation too [i](and who can't blame them!)[/i], but what I can show is some of the progress made about the tree system. [i]Amusement parks in 2089 be like[/i]


Jokes aside, something that we are very proud of is the creation of a system that will let the player give specific items to different characters using dialogues and Yarn Spinner. It was made primarily for a couple of retrieval quest we had in mind, but now with hindsight we may be able to incorporate this new system into other quests.


And that concludes August's devlog. I did promise more content to be shown in the previous one but with most of our team members going on vacation I didn't have much material to work with; hopefully with September we may be able to show more stuff and progress on the game!

notes.title: Nova's Diary 6
notes.content:
Hello friends! 💜

Hope you all are enjoying this summer, between a game and a party.

I apologize in advance if this devlog will be slightly different than the rest, it's because I'm writing this the day before the deadline... (I've been busy with a multitude of things this week)

Nevertheless, let's begin!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/2ccff7e2f089e37ec41c82402c268373e5e3b860.png[/img]
[i]> tfw devlog deadline is tomorrow[/i]


[b]DIALOGUES & STUFF[/b]

Kicking things off as usual with game design, dialogues have been a huge part of production in July; thanks to the new character expressions and the setup of a new Unity scene (thanks Matteo), I've been writing and implementing dialogue like crazy, aswell as adding new expressions and animations to characters.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/1d0279d4a9d7efef998282ea961d8925f40e4f76.gif[/img]
[i]Please ignore the Dr. Octopus cosplayer...[/i]

Another big part of design production this month was the creation of a couple of videos for the event A.MAZE (which, for those who don't know, was a digital event that ran from the 21st to the 24th of July), where also one of our designers actually went to Venice to grab some footage to use.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/1bcc979ffc1a5592b4123583a05593040b2276a1.png[/img]
[i]Francesco and Marina, our lovely designers and video editors[/i]

In the end, the event turned out fine, and all of us resumed working on updating game scenes and discussing about a couple of minor features to be likely added.


[b]2D ART & STUFF[/b]

2D Art has also been very busy this month. For example Ylenia, one of our concept artists, has been working on some props that are pivotal to the main quest of the third day, to then pass on to continuing the work on vibes, namely in game elements that are going to be the triggers for the new vibe system [i](do not worry, I won't stress you with vibes stuff this month)[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/abefbc39e46f645e8d22ccfe915ccc7c49a49621.png[/img]


Our lead artist Federico has been working on Leo's puppet, in order to accomodate future animations and facial expressions. This is something that is probably going to happen to Nova too, so that we won't encounter as many issues as we would now if we ever want or need to rework Nova's character.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/681fb5eef4229133a182ccf0307ed0542b8dd819.png[/img]
[i]Chill Leo do be chillin[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/81610f2b28023dd0728ce1f4289c761c8243cbe7.jpg[/img]
[i]Atleast it doesn't give us any frame issues, so we good?...[/i]

[b]3D ART & STUFF[/b]

And we have a treat for you, TREES! These bad boys are going to be a very important part in our new area, so it's imperative that we create models that are visually coherent with the game world, and actually make sure that they don't create any issue on the technical side of things.  We discovered a very neat system that will help us creating tress, and we're currently testing it to get a feel of what we can tweak.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/1d49b39064c613e25fa1efe81efd0301d3bf73a4.png[/img]
[i]*slaps tree trunk* these bad boys can fit so much oxygen in them[/i]

More structures have also been created alongside the trees. We always thought that the current platforms (the one you see and walk on during the second day) didn't really clicked right, and after a long time they finally got a long overdue rework [i](now with actual platforms as bridges too!) [/i]
We also finalised the work on the new small church, and it is now accompained by a dilapidated tower bell.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/08690b7dab95468a3846223995340f4595b8a1e9.png[/img]


[b]Programming & Stuff[/b]

And finally we get to programming. Apart from general fixes and testing of stuff and features we talked about in the previous months, a highlight of July's production has to be the new VFX for the water puddles. These are one of the vibe triggers that we've talked before.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/be25494c710175b4136b556cd54c01b2c94128b4.gif[/img]
[i]...I don't have any joke here, help[/i]

A new addition to the game is an elevator mechanic, that'll take Nova from their Grandpa's house to the ground [i](and maybe other places too?)[/i]. Still heavily testing so we don't have any actual good image/gif to show here, better luck next month! :)


[i]EVENTS & STUFF[/i]

Not much to say here really, we participated in just a couple of events this month, being the A.MAZE and the DreamHack Beyond [i](which we did yesterday with our super late streaming)[/i]. Funnily enough, yesterday's stream wasn't scheduled for that day. But all things aside, the stream went smooth and in the end we did have fun doing it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/6c7461fa5661018b4dc6d52671ecdd8393ef099f.png[/img]


And that covers all for the month of July. Not really much to add too.
But expect lots of content in August's devlog!

See you next month!

notes.title: Nova's Diary #3
notes.content:
Hello friends, welcome back to Nova’s Diary! ⭐

First of all, if you’re watching this at the time of release,[b] hold on a second[/b]! Because today at 9 PM CEST (so 12pm PT), we’ll hold our final stream of LudoNarraCon on our Community Hub! It’ll be a talk between members of the team, plus we’ll respond to the Q&A forms we posted around the previous days (you can also find it here: https://forms.gle/ZcbCuzLiEZtGeYSt5) 

So yeah, as you can already imagine, this month we worked a lot (and I mean, [i]A LOT[/i]) towards LudoNarraCon. I’m pretty sure this is our biggest event yet and it’s been a blast, technical issues aside. The guys at Fellow Traveler and the other developers are really nice people, and we had tons of fun deciding what we’d show during these 4 days of streams.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/040857d33758b0c3bc9d27634afc013fd17373fd.gif[/img]

But that doesn’t mean that we haven’t worked on Venice tho. For example, our designer better defined the quests of the subsequent days, with a lot more mechanics, characters and interaction for our drone friend! This meant a lot of new tasks to organize, and a better definition of the remaining time of the production.

Our 3D artists worked on creating new buildings for the map, such as little churches and towerbells. We also created some walls and Venetian portici to make the map feel a lot more diverse. We also did some reworking of the roofs, in order to better accommodate high water structures like altane. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/5a78fffaf72f2da3f69835dc55517fd0a3b50dc6.jpg[/img]

As seen during our April 23rd stream, a new character has joined our roster! She’s the Archivist. A character who’s working in Venice’s library in order to preserve the city’s heritage. She’s a bit of a workaholic, and she really cares about her struggle to categorize and preserve every aspect of the city. She’s one of the new characters that Nova will encounter on the third day of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/b1aeabf9436610d4c209d2955b2940db4d7b2cdb.jpg[/img]

Our programmers are developing the new vibe system and we’re all testing and evaluating some new mechanics. To make the vibe collection more satisfying and active, we’re associating specific actions to each kind of vibe! 
For now, we’re testing floating mid-air for a light-hearted mood (yellow), jumping on puddles for feelers (blue), and quicker grinding sequences for speedy players (red). This will take lots of polishing and fine tuning, but so far we’re satisfied with the different interactions they allow with the environment.

Last but absolutely not least, a very important aspect of Nova’s personality that we want to better present is their collecting mania: Nova likes taking physical objects that serve as memories of their experience, and this trip to Venice is no exception.
To better highlight this, we’re developing a camera system that makes these memories more visible, by zooming on the bookshelves in Nova’s room.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/dbd725ffb974a1739c6c803833316e26d9c8fee1.gif[/img]

Aaand that's all for April. It's been a very busy month for the team, yet also extremely rewarding. We'd like to take this time to thank everyone who joined in our streams, who participated in the LudoNarraCon Discord AMA and generally played the game and wishlisted it.

[i]YOU GUYS ARE REAL HEROES[/i]

I have no words to describe how much it helps us, and we can't wait to give back to you once the game will be completed!
Ok, now that's really all. Again, if you're reading this the time of release, remember that at 9 PM CEST (12pm PT) we are going to have our final stream on the Community Hub, where you can ask us anything related to the game or the team. You can find a link to the Google Form at the top of the devlog.
If you want to keep being updated about devlogs and events, follow us on our socials!

See you next time!

notes.title: Nova's Diary #2
notes.content:
Hello friends! 💜

We’re back with our second Nova’s Diary. We have a lot to talk about and a couple of interesting announcements at the end so just sit back, relax, and let’s begin.

[b]A NEW PLAYGROUND[/b]

Last time we teased you a new area of the map, part of our effort to add more days in the game. In this month, Designers and Artists have been working very closely to produce a first version of the new area in Unity.

This is one of the most heavily wrecked neighborhoods in Venice, with lots of abandoned buildings, stray technological elements and generally gives a very neglected vibe. (sorry for the pun)

This area will feature most of the mid-game missions, starting from the third day, where Nova has to help their Grandpa with his statue, and it’ll offer some insight about the more hidden part of the city, thanks to its almost claustrophobic architecture. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/b7a8ea1ed519703bd6df3e1eacfa2565881633f7.png[/img]
[i](Once a crowded residential area of the city, it now lies in ruins) 
[/i]

While the general level design has seen improvements over time, we’ve been also working on defining the new locations and characters Nova will find in their journey. We can’t really tell you much as of yet, so keep an eye out on our socials for more sneak peeks!

(but if you know a little bit of italian you might just make a guess by reading the notes in the art studies below!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/3b930106f22073f41f18f363c096b6bd6605a175.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/b2f71558fe2e5092106c6a469aca540cf60d3e0b.jpg[/img]


[b]MORE EXPRESSIONS![/b]

Our animation department has been working hard to make a lot more animations and expressions for our beloved characters. We loved how grandpa moved while talking to Nova, so we wanted to extend that feeling to each one of our NPCs. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/5e99d1787954432b9a837524b121b0a743523032.gif[/img]


[b]JUST VIBIN'[/b]

As we mentioned in the previous devlog, we wanted to improve the exploration in Venice by tweaking the vibes. This month, our designer and programmers started prototyping the new vibe system. 
We want the act of collecting vibes to feel more active and rewarding, with more complex visual effects that, however, disappear faster. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/339683d21702058ba148451cb9ed0f1cc5ea8179.png[/img]


[b]ANNOUNCEMENT TIME![/b]

Last but not least, we wanted to inform you that, on March 27th, we’ll participate in [b]Now Play This[/b], a festival that will take place starting today the 25th to the 28th, and that will focus on games that explore the topic of climate crisis. 
We’ll also participate in [b]another [/b]festival that still has to be announced, tune in our socials so you won't miss it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/99e2a0b776f463debffb8d4230db050838f4bccc.png[/img]


Aaand that's a wrap for today. We know this is kind of a long read, especially considering this is our second devlog, so let us know if you prefer shorter (maybe more frequent?) devlogs or if you're okay with this format.

As always, thank you for your time and see you next month!

notes.title: Nova's Diary #1
notes.content:
Hello friends! 💜

It’s been a month since our demo landed on Steam, and after a well-deserved short break, we are finally back working on some pretty major aspects of the game. We have a long way ahead of us, with a lot of content to add and systems to improve. 

So we thought: 
[i]"Hey, why don't we show our friends on Steam and on every other platform our progress?"[/i]

And here it is, [b]Nova's Diary[/b]: a monthly column where we'll talk about the main things we've been working on, post sneak peeks and get to know the various members here at Safe Place Studio. 

How about we start with me, the person writing this.

Hi! I'm [b]Giacomo[/b], but you can use my nickname TrustAlpha. I'm the Community Manager of Venice 2089, aswell as its Narrative Designer, meaning that I pretty much have to deal with words 99% of the time. I'm sure there'll be plenty of opportunities in the future to know me aswell as my colleagues, but at least I've introduced myself.



So, lots of things to do. In fact, we want to first and foremost add more days to the game. To do so, we'll need a bigger map! With tons of new interesting places to visit and people to meet. Our artists and designers are working to let you see more and more streets of Venice and capture the magic of the city.
It'll be a while before we can see an actual level design in-game, but here's something to keep you interested!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/e5c43e3a9d18bbd1f25225313ad517fd190528de.png[/img]
[i]Study done by our Concept Artist Federico (Orwellian black&white filter not included)[/i]



Meanwhile, our fellow animators are creating new animations and facial expressions for our beloved characters, in order to make them feel more alive and expressive during gameplay. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/51bb8f121d4a75f0ec5476b7e55e46f97b4418d7.gif[/img]
[i]New trick animation done by our 3D Artist Fabiola. That hoverboard do be spinning doe[/i]



Something we stumbled upon watching you guys play our demo: while riding Nova's hoverboard in Venice is fun and works well for players, we haven't yet achieved our goal of creating a meaningful change in gameplay experience for each play style (are you the active, jumpy type or the contemplative explorer?)
So we're currently reworking vibes (currently the colorful light rings that you find around the map while on the hoverboard) to be more fun to catch, feel more personal, and be more integrated within the game world and how Nova sees it. Get ready for something completely new!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/1ddc193cdb38bc01c75727f9517682aede964b73.png[/img]
[i]Rework concept made by our Game Designer (and blue vibe enthusiast) Marina[/i]


On a last note, we are also updating the dialogue system by using Yarn Spinner, an open-source dialogue editor developed by Secret Lab (and found in games like Night in the Woods). This way, it’ll be easier for us both to add more features and also to make localizations. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39566465/1d50959a57ba84800a375b8887769d00a36dfe3f.png[/img]
[i]Mockup dialogue written by our Game Designer Matteo[/i]


And that's all for our first issue of Nova's Diary, I hope you guys enjoyed it! Feel free to try out our Steam Demo and add us to your wishlist, and remember to follow us for some sneak peek at our (mis)adventures and more devlogs like this. 

See you next time!

notes.title: THE DEMO IS OFFICIALLY OUT!
notes.content:
[i]Hello friends,[/i]

As of now, a new demo of Venice 2089 has become available on Steam. 

We worked hard to improve the experience you had when we first released on itch.io and GameJolt, and thanks to your precious feedback we can now present you a new version of Venice 2089. 

This demo will feature a new level design, a reworked drone and a new musical score. It will also feature long requested additions, like Video Quality Options for lower-end PCs and a series of quality-of-life fixes. 

We sincerely hope you'll like it, and we cannot wait to hear your feedback!
